title: Charat Singh Mounts Foot Soldiers and Fights Across the Flanks

blocks.text: Charat Singh repeatedly throws himself toward whatever side of the caravan is taking the hardest pressure. Whenever the attackers gather in strength, he races there first, cuts down Pathans, and restores just enough space for the caravan to keep moving.

His intervention is practical as well as brave, because captured horses immediately become new mobility for the defenders. After seizing enemy mounts, he mounted many foot soldiers on these so exhausted or dismounted fighters could rejoin the running battle instead of being left behind.

Even while wounded, Charat Singh keeps shifting from flank to flank and maintaining reserve horses for the next charge. The page presents him not only as a fearless fighter but also as the field commander who keeps the Sikh defense coherent while the whole column is under pressure.
